next_mission_recommendation.mission_title: Conductor Observability Dashboard: Parse Failure Analytics and Health Monitoring
next_mission_recommendation.mission_description: Build a real-time observability layer for the hardened conductor. Add a parse failure analytics widget to the AtlasForge dashboard that tracks: (1) parse failure rate per stage over time, (2) synthetic fallback usage frequency and which stages trigger them most, (3) format correction re-prompt success rate (layer 2 saves vs layer 3 fallbacks), (4) raw text pattern analysis to identify common prose drift triggers. Store metrics in SQLite alongside the existing decision_graph.db. Add alerting thresholds: if synthetic fallback rate exceeds 30% in any stage, surface a warning. This data will enable proactive tuning of prompts to reduce prose drift at the source rather than just surviving it.
next_mission_recommendation.rationale: The hardening implemented in this mission is reactive - it survives prose drift but doesn't help prevent it. Observability data on which stages and prompt patterns cause the most parse failures would enable targeted prompt engineering to reduce drift at the source. The dashboard infrastructure already exists (Flask + WebSocket at localhost:5000), so this extends it naturally. Three cycles allow: (1) metrics collection and SQLite schema, (2) dashboard widgets and visualization, (3) alerting and pattern analysis.

final_report.summary: Implemented conductor/runtime hardening to prevent prose-triggered mission death. The root cause was that JSON parse failures in the R&D loop were conflated with transport failures, causing 3 consecutive prose responses to kill a mission via a fatal `break`. The fix introduces a 3-layer hardened parsing pipeline: (1) existing extract_json_from_response, (2) format correction re-prompt to the LLM, (3) deterministic fallback with stage-appropriate synthetic JSON. Parse failures now use a separate counter (MAX_PARSE_FAILURES=5) from transport retries (MAX_CLAUDE_RETRIES=3), emit diagnostics to both journal and chat, and never trigger mission termination. A new response_adapter module provides stage-aware fallbacks for all 6 R&D stages. All synthetic responses are tagged with _synthetic:True for traceability. 17 tests across 3 suites (regression, e2e, adversarial) all pass. One real bug was found during adversarial testing (uncaught extract_fn exceptions) and fixed.

key_achievements: 3-layer hardened parsing pipeline guarantees non-None JSON response for every LLM turn
Separated parse failure counting from transport failure counting - prose responses no longer kill missions
Stage-aware deterministic fallbacks for all 6 R&D stages with conservative defaults (e.g., ANALYZING falls back to needs_revision)
Journal and chat diagnostics on every parse failure with raw text preview for debugging
Graceful degradation when response_adapter module is unavailable (HAS_RESPONSE_ADAPTER guard)
17/17 tests passing across regression, e2e, and adversarial suites
Found and fixed a real bug during adversarial testing: extract_fn exceptions were not caught in adapt_response
challenges_overcome: Identifying the exact root cause: parse failures were conflated with transport failures in the timeout_retries counter
Designing fallback responses that advance the mission safely without making dangerous assumptions (conservative stage transitions)
Ensuring backward compatibility: transport failures still halt correctly, existing extract_json_from_response strategies still work
Adversarial edge cases: null bytes, unicode surrogates, 1MB payloads, deeply nested JSON, XSS payloads all handled safely
lessons_learned: Conflating different failure modes under a single counter is a common source of cascading failures - always use separate counters for semantically different error types
Deterministic fallbacks with traceability markers (_synthetic, _fallback_stage) are safer than 'try harder' retry strategies
Adversarial testing found a real bug that unit and e2e tests missed - always include red-team testing for safety-critical code paths
The format correction re-prompt (layer 2) provides a graceful middle ground between 'parse harder' and 'give up and use synthetic'
